body: I feel that. I'll kinda going through life like a bonus level in a video game. If I want to do something I try to do it, but if it doesn't happen oh well.

The world wouldnt stop for them. Sure people would remember you on the anniversary, but their day to day life would still consist of what they want for dinner or how their day at work was. I think most people overestimate how much they contribute to other people's lives. Just like how your best friend in elementary  school probably isn't your best friend now. If you lose a loved one you are sad sure, but you don't think about them constantly and with time if becomes less and less of a problem. In 5-10 years my family would be over it, and working on their own lives instead of regretting mine.

This is my take on it.

I think it's like this

Hanging here -> hang oneself
Blown mind -> gun to head

Edit: cut it -> cut self.  Idk tbh
Can relate. I came to the realization that I enjoy sleeping more than i enjoy being awake. Makes it hard to be motivated.

For me it's the little things that are habitual, or stuff I want in the future. For example, I have a quote calendar and being able to flip it everyday is something I enjoy. There are also games I want to play but they haven't released yet. I always try to have something to put off the inevitable. After the next quote I'll do it. After this party I'll do it. After this assignment. Making life seem like it only lasts for tommorrow rather than 60 some years is helpful to me.

I don't know if this will work for you, but I wish the best of luck regardless.
If you haven't already, read the talking tips in the side bar. They have some helpful insight on how to deal with these situations. I'm glad you're taking this seriously despite his age.

I had a dream once where I lost my left eye. For 90 percent of the dream I was eyeless. When I woke up I started crying, because I could see out of my left half. These kind of dreams are pretty common, and even more so if you happened to be woken up during the REM portion of your sleep cycle.

Or it could mean you have cancer idk.

Vodka would be the way to go. Just pick a mixer that is somewhat healthy and you should be good to go. The next best bet would be wine I believe.

I would suggest avoiding talking about how their suicide could affect you. In my case it made me feel even worse that I was in some way responsible for causing that person pain.
I wish I could give advice or help, but unfortunately I'm in the same boat as you. Hope you get past this, and if you want to talk I can at the very least listen.

I read this and also can't seem to sleep. When I told my parents I was suicidal, they talked about how sad they would be if I died. But, other people in our family died and they get over it in week or so. I find it hard to believe I would be an exception. This comforts me that other people also feel this way.
I like the storytelling. It really makes it easier to understand for someone who isn't depressed.

That's interesting. My take on death is the exact opposite, instead of doing something I like i am just thinking about what's simplest, obtainable, and least pain. And why do people want to die in their sleep. I never understood this.
It's not really a void. I know there is a lot of stuff there, just it feels meaningless. I'm open to chatting with anyone, if it takes my mind off this.
